correctness.rationale: For each n, Guo et al. Theorem 1 is used with its correct n=k+1 indexing. The square-root-smooth condition forces an exact prime-power component p^a with a>=2 and a unique dominant component, yielding a disjoint exact prime sum. The PNT partial summation contributes constants 2a/(a+1) and 2a/(a-1), with floor/coprimality errors lower order. A uniform sum over all a>=3 is O(X^(2/3)log X), lower order than the a=2 main term. The standalone verifier checks binomial GCDs and exact counts independently; it is not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 GCD criterion determines only nontriviality, leaving the quantitative prevalence and composition of positive-GCD values on the natural critical barrier P^+(n)<=sqrt(n) unspecified. The new theorem yields one exact all-exponent counting framework and a nontrivial hierarchy of power exponents and rational constants, with the unexpected 3/4 dominant scale. It distinguishes prime-factor-driven positive GCDs from higher-prime-power-driven exceptions, a natural structural/statistical invariant rather than a chosen numerical range. The analytic methods are standard and the result does not claim a deeper independent binomial classification.
